Subject: Escape hatch request: lynx-12q p95 tail-latency surge

Hi Kimberly,

We just finished the progressive rollout of lynx-12q to our production traffic at ~50% at 08:50 PST and immediately started seeing our p95 jump from ~230ms to 1.2s for a subset of long-context requests. The attached CSV has a short window (08:52–09:05) showing the spike correlated with the V12q variant.

Business impact: our chat flows for loan-disbursement workflows are timing out or hitting user-facing retry logic (several support tickets already). We need an escape hatch: either a rollback to the previous variant (lynx-11f) or a temporary routing fallback to a non-quantized variant while you investigate.

Questions:
- Can Redwood trigger an emergency variant fallback to lynx-12f (non-quant) for customer Finlytics?
- If we do a rollback/fallback, what should we expect in terms of brief error surface or token cost changes?
- We may also need an SLA exception window and an associated credit if the SLO breach persists — can you advise on the process?

Attaching: lynx-12q_p95_report.csv for the 13-minute window.

Thanks — urgent please.

Subject: Re: Escape hatch request: lynx-12q p95 tail-latency surge

Quick triage notes (initial):
- Observed the same p95 bump on our infra telemetry for requests routed to lynx-12q: CPU latency tail increases when seq length > 1200 tokens. Heap/KV cache warm-up is slower with the new quantized kernels in the rare decoder path.
- The quantization codepath seems to introduce a small additional kernel dispatch for long attention windows; that compounds in the tail.

Mitigation options:
1) Emergency variant fallback to lynx-12f (non-quant). Low risk to model correctness, higher per-token cost but will reduce p95 quickly. We can activate at the routing layer for the Finlytics account only.
2) Canary rollback of lynx-12q to lynx-11f (previous production) — this is a full deploy revert and requires cross-team approvals; expected rollback time ~8–12 minutes and a brief reconnection window for existing sessions. Possible 0.1–0.5% transient error spike during the flip.
3) Traffic cap: throttle Finlytics to 60% throughput and slow the rollout while we push a microfix to the quant kernel. This retains the variant but reduces tail exposure.

I recommend option 1 + option 3 in parallel: activate per-customer fallback to lynx-12f to immediately reduce p95 and cap traffic at 60% so we can collect a broader trace set for debugging. If we see any instability we can perform a controlled rollback.

If you authorize, I'll run the routing change (feature flag) and coordinate with SRE to watch infra. Please confirm authorization and the precise cap percentage.

—Marcus
